text: Python's unpacking lets you pull sequences apart in remarkably flexible ways.
A star in the middle captures everything between the first and last items into a list.
So first grabs one, last grabs five, and middle scoops up everything in between.
[chuckle] Unpacking also gives you the famous one-line swap — no temporary variable needed.
Python evaluates the right side first, then assigns, so a and b trade places instantly.
[sniff] The double-star unpacks dictionaries, letting you merge several into one new dictionary.
Later keys win over earlier ones, and you can add fresh keys right in the same expression.
[sigh] A single star does the same for lists, splicing multiple sequences into one flat list.
[groan] Star and double-star unpacking make merging, splitting, and rearranging data wonderfully concise.
